bibliography.note: PubMed: Microb Ecol. 1993 Nov; 26(3): 201–17 — matches the entry (Crossref lacks the pages)

claims.claim: bacteria hold 33.1 fg C per cell
claims.note: No full text. The abstract gives 'the empirically measured factor converting bacterial biomass to carbon was 0.36 pg C µm⁻³ or 33.1 fg C cell⁻¹' (a growth experiment on Lake Pääjärvi bacteria; the per-cell figure implies a mean cell volume near 0.09 µm³).

claims.claim: in mesohumic Lake Pääjärvi bacterial production was 1.8–13.2 µg C/L/d in the growing season and 0.2–2.9 in winter, 19–33 % of primary production (cited as abstract only)
claims.note: The abstract gives these numbers; the 19–33 % is 'in the epilimnion … on average'. Samples 1991–1992 from a bay of Lake Pääjärvi, southern Finland (per Tulonen's 2004 thesis summary).

claims.claim: Bird & Kalff's count at chlorophyll 3–5 µg/L × 33.1 fg C per cell ≈ 57–85 µg C/L (project estimate)
claims.note: The arithmetic holds: 10^(5.867 + 0.776·log10 3) = 1.73 × 10⁶ cells/mL × 33.1 fg = 57 µg C/L; at 5 µg/L, 2.57 × 10⁶ → 85 µg C/L. The Tulonen input is unchecked (abstract only); applying one lake's carbon-per-cell factor to other lakes' counts is the project's extrapolation.
